exam: JPSC Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination 2025 (Advt. No. 01/2026)
paper: General Studies Paper-II (Jharkhand GK) - Question Booklet Series A (held 19.04.2026)

questions.q: Which fish has been declared as state fish of Jharkhand?
questions.e: Desi Mangur (Clarias magur) was declared the state fish of Jharkhand.

questions.q: The Valmiki Yojana in Jharkhand Budget 2025-26 provides a monthly stipend of ____
questions.e: As per the official key, the Valmiki scheme in the 2025-26 state budget offers a monthly stipend of ₹4,000.

questions.q: Who is the author of the book 'Prem me Ped hona'?
questions.e: 'Prem Mein Ped Hona' is a poetry collection by Jasinta Kerketta.

questions.q: Bhagwan Birsa Munda excellence Award 2024 was given to ____
questions.e: As per the official key, Dr. Arpana Sharma received the Bhagwan Birsa Munda Excellence Award 2024.

questions.q: The Jharkhand budget is primarily spent on :
questions.e: Social welfare (including social sector schemes) takes the largest share of Jharkhand's budget, per the official key.

questions.q: Who became the first female DGP in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Tadasha Mishra was appointed Jharkhand's first woman DGP (in-charge) in 2025.

questions.q: As of mid-2024, how many panchayats in Jharkhand have been declared tuberculosis free?
questions.e: As per the official key, 38 panchayats were declared TB-free by mid-2024.

questions.q: In which year was Manki Munda scholarship launched?
questions.e: The Manki Munda Scholarship for tribal students was launched in 2024.

questions.q: Palash Brand is for empowering whom?
questions.e: Palash is JSLPS's brand for products made by rural and tribal women's self-help groups.

questions.q: When was the Tejaswini Yojana approved by the World Bank?
questions.e: The World Bank approved the Tejaswini adolescent girls project for Jharkhand on 21 June 2016.

questions.q: What is the Objective of ARYA Yojana?
questions.e: ARYA (Attracting and Retaining Youth in Agriculture) aims to draw rural youth into farming.

questions.q: When was "Phoolon Jhano Ashirvad Abhiyan" launched in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Phulo Jhano Ashirwad Abhiyan, to help women leave liquor-making for livelihoods, was launched in September 2020.

questions.q: How many Industrial Area Development Authorities are working in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Jharkhand has four Industrial Area Development Authorities (Ranchi, Adityapur, Bokaro, Santhal Pargana).

questions.q: When was the first industrial policy of Jharkhand declared?
questions.e: Jharkhand announced its first Industrial Policy in 2001.

questions.q: In which Five-Year plan was Bokaro steel plant established?
questions.e: Bokaro Steel Plant was set up in 1964, during the Third Five-Year Plan.

questions.q: Where is Hindalco Aluminium Industry?
questions.e: Hindalco's alumina refinery is at Muri in Ranchi district.

questions.q: When was Tata Iron and Steel Company established?
questions.e: Jamsetji Tata's TISCO was established at Jamshedpur in 1907.

questions.q: Where is the fertilizer factory located in Jharkhand?
questions.e: The Fertilizer Corporation's plant was located at Sindri (Dhanbad).

questions.q: What is the amount of Rehabilitation grants (immediate)?
questions.e: As per the official key, the immediate rehabilitation grant is ₹2.5 lakh.

questions.q: Under the Rehabilitation policy, who is the chairman of the District Level Rehabilitation Committee?
questions.e: The Deputy Commissioner chairs the District Level Rehabilitation Committee.

questions.q: What is the main objective of forming ‘Economic Zone’ in case of displacement and rehabilitation in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Economic zones for displaced persons aim to encourage industrial investment while providing livelihoods.

questions.q: Which sports person from Jharkhand got Arjuna Award in 2024?
questions.e: Hockey player Salima Tete from Simdega received the Arjuna Award in 2024.

questions.q: Where is Shaheed Nirmal Mahto Stadium?
questions.e: Shaheed Nirmal Mahto Stadium is in Jamshedpur.

questions.q: What was the mascot of the 4th South Asian Athletics Championships 2025?
questions.e: 'Dalma' was the mascot of the 4th South Asian Athletics Championships held in Ranchi in 2025.

questions.q: Rupa Rani Tirkey and Lovely Chaubey are related to which sports?
questions.e: Rupa Rani Tirkey and Lovely Choubey are Commonwealth Games gold medallists in lawn bowls.

questions.q: How many medals did Jharkhand win in the 38th National Games held in Dehradun, Uttarakhand?
questions.e: As per the official key, Jharkhand won 25 medals at the 38th National Games.

questions.q: Which of the following climatic regions are available in Jharkhand according to Koppen's scheme
questions.e: Most of Jharkhand is Cwg (monsoon with dry winter) with Aw (tropical savanna) in parts.

questions.q: Which of the following Hot water springs is present in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Tatapani/Tetulia is among the hot springs found in Jharkhand, per the official key.

questions.q: Which is the Calm period in the Geological History of Jharkhand?
questions.e: As per the official key, the Cambrian-Ordovician-Silurian periods were a calm period in Jharkhand's geological history.

questions.q: Give the correct option regarding the formation period of Damodar River Valley
questions.e: The Damodar valley's Gondwana coal basins formed between the Devonian and Permian periods (per the official key).

questions.q:
Which is the correct sequence of the under-mentioned Research institutions according to their establishment period:
i) Indian Lac Research Institute, Ranchi
ii) Central Fuel Research Institute, Jealgora
iii) Central Mining Research Institute, Dhanbad
questions.e: Indian Lac Research Institute (1925), Central Fuel Research Institute (1946), Central Mining Research Institute (1956).

questions.q: What is the percentage range of Forest area in Jharkhand at present?
questions.e: Jharkhand's recorded forest/tree cover is roughly 29-33% of its area; the key gives 20-30 percent.

questions.q: Which is the largest forest area in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Protected forests form the largest share of Jharkhand's recorded forest area.

questions.q: After bifurcation of Bihar which two tribes are being merged in Jharkhand?
questions.e: As per the official key, Sabar and Hill Kharia were the tribes merged/added after the state's creation.

questions.q: Which is the leading producing mineral in Singhbhum?
questions.e: Singhbhum is Jharkhand's leading iron ore producing region.

questions.q: Where is Jharkhand's first floating solar power plant located?
questions.e: Jharkhand's first floating solar plant was set up on Dimna/related waters near Jamshedpur, per the official key.

questions.q: Which dam was constructed at first under Damodar Valley corporation projects?
questions.e: Tilaiya Dam (1953) on the Barakar was the first dam built by the Damodar Valley Corporation.

questions.q: When did the concept of Damodar Valley project germinate in the mind of administration
questions.e: The DVC concept took shape after the devastating 1943 Damodar flood.

questions.q: Promotion of Extremism in Joint Bihar/Jharkhand was started from which district?
questions.e: Per the official key, extremism in joint Bihar/Jharkhand began from Jahanabad.

questions.q: Jharkhand is divided into three seismic zones; which one is correct?
o: Damodar Valley - Very low affected area; North Jharkhand - Low affected area; Southern Jharkhand - Medium affected area
Damodar Valley - Low affected area; North Jharkhand - Medium affected area; Southern Jharkhand - Very low affected area
Damodar Valley - Medium affected area; North Jharkhand - Very low affected area; Southern Jharkhand - Low affected area
Damodar Valley - Low affected area; North Jharkhand - Very low affected area; Southern Jharkhand - Medium affected area
questions.e: As per the official key: Damodar valley - low, North Jharkhand - medium, Southern Jharkhand - very low seismic hazard.

questions.q: What are correct activities for soil management:
o: Soil management requires attention in - 1) Soil Temperature 2) Soil Moisture 3) Soil Air
Soil management requires attention in - 1) Soil Acidity 2) Soil Productivity 3) Soil Erosion
Soil management requires attention in - 1) Intensive tillage 2) Monocropping 3) Over fertilization
Soil management requires attention in - 1) Living fallow 2) Burning crop residues 3) Soil sterilization
questions.e: Soil management focuses on soil acidity, productivity and erosion.

questions.q: In which district is soil erosion higher in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Per the official key, soil erosion is highest in Dhanbad district, a mining-affected area.

questions.q: What is the correct status of Fallow land for last five years in Jharkhand?
o: Percentage of fallow land is not changing
questions.e: Per the official key, the share of fallow land has been increasing in recent years.

questions.q: According to the report of Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) 2019-2021 on the basis of BOD Which river is more polluted
questions.e: As per the official key, the Subarnarekha was assessed as the most polluted by BOD in the CPCB 2019-21 report.

questions.q: Which fruit has comparatively more growing area in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Mango occupies the largest fruit-growing area in Jharkhand.

questions.q: Mark the correct figure regarding the Jharkhand’s Urbanisation rate 2011.
questions.e: Jharkhand's urban population share in Census 2011 was 24.05 percent.

questions.q: Mark the correct figure of literacy rate in Jharkhand during 2011 census?
questions.e: Jharkhand's literacy rate in Census 2011 was 66.41 percent.

questions.q: Which one is the correct figure regarding the Tribal population growth in Jharkhand during 1901 and 2011 census respectively?
questions.e: As per the official key, tribal population grew from about 18.29 lakh (1901) to 86.45 lakh (2011).

questions.q: Which one is the correct figure regarding the population growth in Jharkhand during 1901 and 2011 census respectively?
questions.e: Jharkhand's population rose from about 60.68 lakh in 1901 to 329.88 lakh in 2011.

questions.q: When was the 'Mukhyamantri Jan Van Yojna’ launched in Jharkhand?
questions.e: The Mukhyamantri Jan Van Yojana for planting on private land was launched in 2015-16.

questions.q: How many National Parks are there in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Betla in Palamu is Jharkhand's only national park.

questions.q: How many sanctuaries are there in Jharkhand?
questions.e: As per the official key, Jharkhand has 12 wildlife sanctuaries.

questions.q: Identify the types of forest in Jharkhand?
questions.e: Jharkhand's forests are tropical (dry and moist deciduous).

questions.q: Who is author of 'Nagpuri Fag Shatak'?
questions.e: 'Nagpuri Phag Shatak' was written by Ghasiram, a noted Nagpuri poet.

questions.q: The deity named 'Dharmesh' is included among the deities of which of the following tribal communities?
questions.e: Dharmes is the supreme deity of the Oraon tribe.

questions.q: In 1983, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha was divided into how many groups?
questions.e: In 1983 the JMM split into two factions.

questions.q: Who among the following was the promulgator of the 'Tribal Panchsheel'?
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru set out the 'Tribal Panchsheel' principles for tribal development.

questions.q: Which of the following dance forms involves only ladies?
questions.e: Domkach is performed by women, especially during weddings.

questions.q: The Inter-village Panchayat assembly called Bhira was related to which of the following tribal communities?
questions.e: Bhira is the inter-village council of the Hill Kharia.

questions.q: Who among the following was made the first speaker of Jharkhand Assembly in 2000 CE?
questions.e: Inder Singh Namdhari was the first Speaker of the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly (2000).

questions.q: For which among the following communities was enacted in 1947 the Act of returning Agricultural Land in lieu of its major involvement in Non-cooperation movement?
questions.e: The Tana Bhagat Raiyats Agricultural Land Restoration Act, 1947 returned lands lost by Tana Bhagats during the freedom struggle.

questions.q: Beniram Mahatha, a celebrated personality was mainly related to which field?
questions.e: Beniram Mahatha is known as a Nagpuri literary figure.

questions.q: Vachaspati Tripathi was arrested during which movements?
questions.e: Vachaspati Tripathi was arrested during the Quit India Movement.

questions.q: How many districts of Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh were sought during the 1920s to make a separate Jharkhand state?
questions.e: The 1920s demand for Jharkhand covered 16 districts of Bihar, Odisha, Bengal and MP, per the official key.

questions.q: Which among the following Jharkhand Brahmans did not perform the jobs of Purohitas?
questions.e: Per the official key, Sarwar (Sarwariya) Brahmans did not perform priestly duties.

questions.q: Pande Bhava Rai was Diwan of who among the following.
questions.e: Pande Bhava Rai was Diwan of Nagvanshi king Phani Mukut Rai.

questions.q: 'Manjhi Sthan', the place of Panchayat, is mainly related to which tribal community?
questions.e: Manjhi Than is the village council place of the Santhals.

questions.q: The Dhokolo Sohor administrative system is mainly related to which of the following tribes?
questions.e: Dhokolo Sohor is the traditional governance system of the Kharia.

questions.q: Who among the following was political head of Paraha?
questions.e: Per the official key, the Manki is the political head of the Parha.

questions.q: The Mod Manjhi was Panchayat of how many Manjhis?
questions.e: Mod Manjhi is the council of five Manjhis, per the official key.

questions.q: In the Paraha system, which of the following called meetings (Baithak) of the Panchayat?
questions.e: In the Parha system the Pande convenes Panchayat meetings, per the official key.

questions.q: On the instruction of Munda, which of the following spread information in the village?
questions.e: The Kotwar spreads information in the village on the Munda's instruction.

questions.q: Which Royal dynasty introduced the term ‘Bhuinhar’ for the traditional community headman?
questions.e: The Nagvanshi dynasty introduced the term 'Bhuinhar' for traditional headmen.

questions.q: Who is the author of the story 'Puna Khor'?
questions.e: Per the official key, 'Puna Khor' is a story by Indrajeet Oraon.

questions.q: Who among the following has got the ‘Padmashri' Award?
questions.e: Bhagavat Murmu received the Padma Shri, per the official key.

questions.q: A.K. Jha of Bokaro is a noted writer of which language?
questions.e: A.K. Jha of Bokaro is known for his writings in Khortha.

questions.q: Who is the author of 'Ravan Vadha'?
questions.e: Per the official key, 'Ravan Vadh' was written by Chandramohan Mahato.

questions.q: How many stories are there in the work ‘Aea Nav kaniko' by Ram Dayal Munda?
questions.e: Per the official key, Ram Dayal Munda's work contains seven stories.

questions.q: The conical hutment called 'Kumba' was used by which of the following tribal communities?
questions.e: The nomadic Birhor live in conical leaf huts called 'Kumba'.

questions.q: The Chutia Ram Temple was built in which year
questions.e: The Chutia Ram temple (Ram-Sita temple) was built in 1685 by Nagvanshi king Raghunath Shah.

questions.q: Which of the following is 'Ramkathi'?
questions.e: Per the official key, 'Ramkathi' is a musical instrument.

questions.q: Which of the following dances is performed on the day after Diwali?
questions.e: Sohrai, the cattle and harvest festival dance, is performed the day after Diwali.

questions.q: Under Santal Parganas Tenancy Act, 1949, Santal Parganas division is composed of
questions.e: Santhal Pargana division comprises Dumka, Sahibganj, Godda, Deoghar (with Pakur and Jamtara).

questions.q: From a constitutional stand point, the Santal paragnas Act, 1949 is most closely linked with
questions.e: The SPT Act protects tribal land in Scheduled Areas, linking it to Article 244 (Fifth Schedule).

questions.q: Under the Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, transfer of tribal land to non-tribals is:
questions.e: The CNT Act prohibits transfer of tribal land to non-tribals, with limited exceptions.

questions.q: Which authority has the power under Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act, 1908 to restore illegally transferred tribal land?
questions.e: Under CNT Act Section 71A the Deputy Commissioner can restore illegally transferred tribal land.

questions.q: The Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act, 1908 ; recognises which of the following tenure system.
questions.e: The CNT Act recognises Mundari Khuntkatti tenure.

questions.q: Under the Santal Parganas Tenancy Act, 1949 restoration of alienated tribal land
questions.e: Restoration of alienated tribal land under the SPT Act is generally mandatory.

questions.q: Which authority plays the most decisive role in enforcement of the Santal Parganas Tenancy Act, 1949
questions.e: The Deputy Commissioner is the key authority enforcing the SPT Act.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly explains the significance of PESA, 1996 in Jharkhand?
o: It strengthens Gram Sabha control over local resources
It transfers power from state to centre
questions.e: PESA 1996 empowers Gram Sabhas in Scheduled Areas over local resources.

questions.q: Saranda forest region often in news, is significant because :
o: It is India's largest tiger reserve
Supreme Court direction to declare wildlife sanctuary
It lies entirely in non-scheduled area
questions.e: Saranda was in news after Supreme Court directions to declare it a wildlife sanctuary.

questions.q: Which colonial authority enacted the Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act, 1908?
questions.e: The CNT Act 1908 was passed by the Bengal legislative council under the Governor-General in Council's authority, per the official key.

questions.q: The concept of "Khuntkatti" under the Chota Nagpur Tenancy Act, 1908 implies:
o: Individual ownership created by the state
Collective village ownership without cultivation rights
Joint ancestral ownership based on first reclamation
questions.e: Khuntkatti is joint ancestral ownership of land by the descendants of those who first cleared it.

questions.q: The strict Provisions of the Santal Paraganas Tenancy Act, 1949 are best understood in the context of
questions.e: The SPT Act's strict protections arose from tribal revolts (like the Hul) and land alienation.
